blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Primary effects occur directly due to the hazard event itself, such as ground shaking, surface faulting, and immediate structural collapse.
Secondary effects are indirect consequences triggered by primary impacts, including landslides, tsunamis, fires, and soil liquefaction.
While primary effects cause immediate localized damage, secondary effects often spread across larger regions and extend over longer durations.
Effective disaster risk reduction requires dual mitigation strategies that address both direct structural vulnerabilities and secondary post-disaster hazards.

blocks.content: Primary effects cause immediate physical destruction, while secondary effects propagate long-term socio-economic and environmental disruptions.

rows: Occur immediately during the occurrence of the hazard
Occur after the initial event (hours, days, or weeks later)
Direct result of the physical hazard itself
Triggered as a result of primary damage or disruption
Building collapse, ground rupture, surface displacement
Landslides, tsunamis, soil liquefaction, fires, epidemics
Early warning systems, land-use zoning, emergency response

items: Tsunamis, landslides, post-earthquake fires, and soil liquefaction are frequently tested as classic secondary effects in competitive exams.
Direct structural collapse, ground rupture, and surface displacement are categorized strictly as primary effects.
Questions often evaluate candidates on distinguishing direct physical hazards from indirect socio-economic impacts.
